place: London's ground sliced open under the streets at night, old Tube tunnels glowing in the clay
the face of the new tunnel, a cutterhead spinning toward them

moments.what: the cutaway of London's ground glows, streets and buildings on top, the spinning cutterhead nosing in, its name written beside it
a bright line of new tunnel grows behind the cutterhead
street lamps and windows light along the surface
the camera glides down into the clay as the old Tube tunnels light one by one, trains sliding through
close on the cutterhead, the Tube tunnel in its path glowing amber

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Crossrail dug a railway between London's Tube tunnels.

params.place: the new tunnel seen side-on, the whole machine laid out inside it

moments.what: the cutterhead spins close, sparks of clay flying
the camera pulls back from the cutterhead along the shield
a dimension bracket runs the machine's full length and its figure counts up
the trailing gantries light one after another
concrete rings appear behind the machine's tail
the cutterhead turns and the machine creeps forward one step
the bracket's figure counts up as the camera keeps pulling back
the finished tunnel lights behind the tail

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: How? Its machines were 150 metres long, and each built the tunnel as it dug.

params.place: the cutting face: the clay wall, the wheel pressed against it

moments.what: the camera swings round to face the cutterhead
a label writes on: cutterhead
the wheel spins faster, its cutting discs catching the light
clay crumbles off the face in chunks
a bracket spans the wheel
the hole's figure lands on the bracket

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: At the front, a steel wheel spins into the clay, cutting a hole 7.1 metres across.

params.place: inside the shield, cut open: the sealed chamber behind the wheel

moments.what: the ground above the machine cracks
loose clay trickles from the roof
the shield turns see-through and the chamber behind the wheel shows
clay chunks pour into the chamber and fill it
the chamber's back wall glows: a sealed bulkhead
pressure arrows push out into the face, and the cracks close

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Why doesn't the ground cave in? Dug clay fills a sealed chamber that pushes back.

params.place: along the back-up gantries, the conveyor running the machine's length

moments.what: close on the full chamber, clay spilling at its floor
the screw starts turning
the screw lifts clay up onto the belt
the belt lights and starts moving
clay lumps ride the belt
the camera tracks the clay back along the gantries
pull back: the belt runs the machine's whole length into the finished tunnel

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Where does it go? A conveyor carries the clay back along the machine.

params.place: the tail of the machine, looking down the tunnel where the ring is built

moments.what: the camera reaches the machine's tail
a yellow erector arm swings up
it lifts a curved concrete segment
the segment clicks into place with a flash
the last pieces close the ring
the camera pulls back down the tunnel: ring after ring lines it
the segment swings up toward the ring's gap

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: At the back, an arm bolts concrete pieces into a ring, lining the tunnel.

place: central London from above, the tunnel lines drawn under it

moments.what: hydraulic jacks push against the new ring
the whole machine slides forward one step
the cutterhead turns again
cut to above London: the tunnel lines growing under the streets
glowing machine heads lead each line
a counter on the line counts up
the glowing heads race ahead along the lines
the river and street grid light across the map
the newest ring flashes as the rams press on it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It pushes off each ring and creeps forward. Together, the machines dug 42 kilometres under London.

place: the streets above the line, every building tagged with a sensor
Tottenham Court Road station, the Northern line tunnel below

moments.what: sensor dots light on the buildings
rail lines light
pipes under the street light
the counter of checked things counts up on a monitoring screen
a sensor needle trembles and holds still
cut down to the station: the platform tunnels in the clay
the Northern line tunnel glows, a train sliding through
the new machine's cutterhead arrives just above it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Over 17,000 buildings, rails and pipes were checked for movement. At Tottenham Court Road, the Northern line was already there.

params.place: between the two tunnels, the thin band of clay over the Northern line

moments.what: the new tunnel's cutterhead slides in above the Northern line tunnel
the camera tracks beside it
the clay between the tunnels thins
a bracket spans the gap
the gap's figure slams onto the bracket in amber
the new tunnel's rings glow behind the cutterhead
the bracket's ticks pulse as the figure's unit writes on

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The new tunnel passed over it with just 700 millimetres to spare.

params.place: pulling back out through the clay to London's ground sliced open

moments.what: the new tunnel lights along its length
the camera pulls back up through the clay
the streets and buildings light on top
the old Tube tunnels glow around the new one, the cutterhead spinning as in the first frame

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: A new line, threaded between the old ones.

disclaimer: Animations are simplified illustrations, not exact to scale.
